task_specification.objective: Close the Warden self-occlusion regression with direct, non-destructive costume isolation and make native dense-performance and complete ordinary-run release qualification directly recapturable without changing the preserved cemetery, camera composition, Warden rig, combat systems, HUD family, or terminal transaction.

diagnosis.root_cause: The remaining presentation regression is no longer a world-geometry or camera-follow defect: the accepted Warden's own oversized Mage_Hat dominates its projected silhouette, while the authored 41-bone animation remains valid underneath. Nine prior treatments concentrated on camera transforms, containment, and world-occluder compositing, so another framing adjustment would repeat a disproven strategy. The dense-performance and complete-run checks remain failed primarily because the candidate does not yet expose one bounded, candidate-bound matrix that the host can drive and distinguish from diagnostic routes; prior evidence demonstrated a 32-enemy software-renderer profile and isolated lifecycle behavior, but not the native 3/5/10/18/final-wave sequence or uninterrupted ordinary-run matrix.

stop_conditions: Do not modify, extract, replace, or destructively edit the accepted KayKit Warden source package, skeleton, authored animations, lantern attachment, cemetery package, or imported child meshes.

Do not return to camera-transform, FOV, character-scale, or world-occluder tuning for the hat regression; stop and report if direct wrapper-level hat isolation cannot preserve the accepted body, lantern, and telegraph presentation.

Do not tune gameplay budgets or claim 60 FPS from a software renderer. If a native 1920x1080 renderer is unavailable, finish only the truthful candidate-side profile matrix and leave the performance verdict to Runtime and Tester.
Diagnostic preparation may establish stable inspection states but must never satisfy an ordinary-route, complete-run, build-shape, failure, victory, replay, or release row.
Do not treat the deferred stale input-context issue or any backlog gap as current implementation scope.
Stop implementation after all three bounded surfaces are candidate-ready and preserve native project boot; formal issue closure and phase closure remain Tester and GameLoop Runtime responsibilities.

strategy.rationale: Use a materially different root-cause treatment: isolate only the Warden's self-occluding hat at the existing presentation wrapper instead of moving the camera, character, cemetery, or authored rig. In parallel, separate dense-profile and complete-run qualification into generation-bound candidate ledgers whose prepared and advanced states are explicit, whose diagnostic routes cannot masquerade as ordinary play, and whose native evidence remains host-owned.

code: Import and parse the candidate with the frozen Godot version; require no fatal resource, scene, or GDScript errors.

Run focused assertions for hat-binding resolution and restoration, animation/terminal ownership invariants, profile prepare-versus-advance separation, generation matching, release-build fixture guards, and ordinary-versus-diagnostic ledger rejection.
Re-run native_godot_project and host_godot_boot preservation checks after the bounded changes.
runtime: Runtime/Tester: from Title, capture ordinary locomotion and the held Cheer checkpoint from the shipped camera, then repeat the same presentation check at 25–40-enemy density; pair frames with Warden animation, hat-isolation, lantern, terminal lease, VFX, audio, and Result-commit state.

Runtime/Tester: on a native non-software renderer at 1920x1080, execute the 3/5/10/18 workload samples and the representative 32-enemy-plus-Bellkeeper sample, collecting p50/p95/p99/max frame time, physics time, workload caps, logs, and three reset cycles.

Runtime/Tester: perform uninterrupted ordinary failure and victory runs, three natural build-shape runs, Credits & Notices traversal, Result verification, Retry, replay, and Return to Title; require ordinary route predicates and candidate-bound ledger rows for every claimed cell.

Verify title, Play, W movement, Space dash, Escape pause/resume, Retry, and Return to Title still route through their ordinary input contexts, and confirm editor-only fixture actions are unavailable in a release export context.
visual: Compare same-framing shipped-camera locomotion and held-Cheer frames: the Warden's body, attached lantern, and major limb pose must read clearly without the hat dominating the silhouette.

Inspect representative dense combat from the shipped camera for player/telegraph separation, preserved cemetery composition, cool moonlight and warm lantern hierarchy, and absence of new masking artifacts.

Capture the ordinary title, dense final wave with Bellkeeper, failure Result, victory Result, and Credits & Notices states needed for the complete-run matrix; use screenshots as presentation evidence only when paired with authoritative runtime state.

done_when: The runtime resolves the concrete self-occluding hat geometry through the accepted Warden instance and applies a presentation-only shipped-camera isolation policy without changing the imported GLB, skeleton, animation mappings, character/root transforms, lantern socket, or camera transform.

Ordinary idle and locomotion plus the held victory/Cheer checkpoint retain valid authored animation ownership, 41-bone deformation, one terminal lease, one VFX onset, one victory-audio authorization, and exactly one Result commit.
